context: The item is a used smartphone in good condition.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I'm looking for a used smartphone, but I know how sellers love to inflate prices with exaggerated descriptions. Let's skip the markup games and sales fluff—I'm offering 60 for it.

Seller ($185): Honestly, offering 60 breaks my heart considering I'm only selling my prized phone to cover urgent medical bills for my family. I actually have another buyer coming in 30 minutes willing to pay full price, but I can reluctantly hold it for you if you offer 185 right now.
Buyer ($60): Guilt trips about medical bills and phantom buyers arriving in 30 minutes are textbook pressure tactics. Since you haven't offered a genuine reduction, my offer stays firm at 60.

Seller ($165): It deeply pains me that you think I'm lying while I'm already practically giving away my personal memories just to get by. Look, the other person just messaged saying they're stuck in traffic, so if you can meet me at 165 within the next ten minutes, I will reluctantly let you have it.

Buyer ($95): Another artificial ten-minute deadline won't panic me into a bad deal, but since you actually lowered your price to 165, I'll show some movement. I'm willing to raise my offer to 95, so let's see if you can be reasonable.

Seller ($150): Offering 95 feels like a cruel insult when I am forced to part with my personal belongings today just to pay emergency costs. I shouldn't do this, but out of absolute desperation, I will reluctantly lower my price to my rock-bottom limit of 150 if you pay immediately. Please take it right now before the traffic clears for the other buyer.
Buyer ($150): Cut the dramatic sob story, but since you finally dropped your price below my threshold to 150, I'll take it. I accept your offer. <AGREEMENT>
